name: What happens if structural damage is found after demolition starts?

mainEntity.name: What if hidden structural damage is discovered during a remodel after the walls are opened?
mainEntity.text: What if hidden structural damage is discovered during a remodel after the walls are opened?

acceptedAnswer.text: Hidden structural problems are common in older homes and during major remodeling. Once drywall or flooring is removed, contractors may discover dry rot, termite damage, cracked framing, sagging joists, prior DIY alterations, or outdated structural members that no longer meet current expectations for safety and performance. When that happens, the project should pause so the issue can be documented and evaluated. The contractor or engineer may need to revise the design, order new materials, and update the permit if the repair affects the approved scope. Homeowners should expect some contingency budget in any structural remodel because unknown conditions are part of the process, especially in homes with past additions or water intrusion. A clear change-order process and rapid communication are important so the repair does not stall the entire job. This is a common search because people want to know whether a surprise finding will derail the remodel or simply become a managed adjustment.
acceptedAnswer.description: Work should stop in the affected area until the damage is assessed and the repair plan is updated. Hidden rot, termite damage, undersized framing, or previous unpermitted work can change the scope, price, and permit requirements before construction resumes.
